6. NearPod

Founded: 2012

G2 rating: 4.6/5 Stars (114 reviews)

NearPod is a student-engagement platform that allows students, teachers, and higher education institutions to engage and evaluate students using collaborative discussions and interactive virtual classes. Administrators can deliver important lessons manually in different formats and customize them or use the lessons available to improve the overall learning experience. This cloud-based platforms also features a social learning module for instructors to run gamified lessons for peer interactions and competition.

- NearPod is a perfect platform for teachers to prepare interactive sessions to engage students. It has tools like gamified activities, videos, and live participation.

- Integrate with third party applications and learning management systems like Canvas, Google Classroom, Blackboard, Schoology, etc.

- NearPod features school-based, hybrid, and home-based learning modules including student insights, online learning, pre-built lessons, and other interesting tools.

- Measure students’ progress and understanding with real-time assessments and checks. Teachers can collect insights during and even after lessons to understand individual student’s progress.

- Use existing resources to make them more interactive by uploading content from Google Slides, PowerPoint, YouTube, and other platforms.

NearPod is an excellent learning and assessment platform that encourages learning management, assessment management, course management, and reporting/analytics.

7. FlexiQuiz

Founded: 2015

G2 rating: 4.5/5 Stars (2 reviews)

FlexiQuiz is an online platform assessment and quiz maker platform. It allows users to create customized tests for customers, students, and employees. Companies can either publish the assessments privately for their community or publicly for any registrant.

The software grades assessments automatically. The platform is designed with several configurable features and ease of use to assist users to create engaging tests, courses, or quizzes. It offers 8 types of question templates, progress bars, time limits, question banks, notifications, certificates, and the feature to add images, videos, audio, and video to the content. It also has a powerful reporting tool to view data.

Pros

- This easy-to-use interface helps in building customized tests and quizzes without coding knowledge. It also offers templates of question types and some formatting options for building quizzes.

- Choose from a set of 8 pre-defined types of questions, such as essay, fill-in-the-blanks, multiple choice questions, file upload, picture choice, and matching text, to create formal examinations or trivia quizzes.

- Manage branding with design using the latest options to customize background images and color, logos, navigation buttons, page layouts, and much more.

- Have better control over the grading system by defining the number of points to be awarded per question or for each answer. Users can define the minimum scores to pass a test.

FlexiQuiz is popular for its active dashboard, flexibility, reporting, learning management, assessment management, and statistics.

8. EdApp

Founded: 2018

G2 rating: 4.7/5 Stars (215 reviews)

EdApp is an award-winning, cloud-based free mobile learning management solution (LMS). It is used to train teams, both large and small, across every industrial domain worldwide. It features an integrated authoring tool, learner app, and editable content library, designed for the digital habits of modern times. With built-in concepts like gamification, spaced repetition, push notifications, and AI translation, EdApp makes learning more engaging and fun, thus giving higher retention with deeper knowledge.

- EdApp is a powerful authoring tool that is easy to deploy and use

- It has some impressive built-in features like Canva integration, PowerPoint conversion, and cloud-based translation.

- It translates the courseware automatically into more than 100 languages within a few clicks in minutes.

- It creates bespoke graphics and tracks results through advanced analytics.

- It integrates seamlessly with SABA, Zapier, Cornerstone, SAP, and SumTotal.

EdApp also supports user group management together with real prizing and gamification to promote engagement and drive results. Social learning is an interesting feature that allows users to add comments on the courses and submit their suggestions/ideas, and interact with other team members.

9. Vervoe

Founded: 2016

G2 rating: 4.6/5 Stars (64 reviews)

Vervoe is a recruitment management solution for businesses. It manages hiring, assessment and screening through video interviews, skills tests, assessments, and more. The platform features white-label capabilities, which allows companies to design a custom portal using the company logo and establish a brand identity.

Pros

- Tests soft skills, mindset, technical ability with custom tests and on-the-job tests.

- Create role-based tests using audio, code tests, video, text, file upload and download, and MCQs.

- Post requirements to job boards and relevant social networks, promote company values and culture to candidates.

- Track real-time status updates while candidates are moving through their hiring journey.

- Integrates with third-party apps like Comeet, SmartRecruiter, Workday, PageUp, Zapier, and more.

Vervoe’s assessment library helps recruiters create an array of custom assessments including text, videos, MCQs, on-the-job tasks, technical skills and soft skills. It also includes document editing, trackable job links, audio recording, candidate pool, auto candidate progression/rejection, and more. Its AI-enabled algorithm rank and grade candidates based on performance.

10. Codility

Founded: 2009

G2 rating: 4.6/5 Stars (408 reviews)

Codility is one of the finest remote hiring platforms for engineering teams. Experts can use this platform to forecast real-life skills of technical candidates at different stages of hiring, through relevant and unbiased assessments like CodeCheck, virtual recruitment events or CodeEvent, live technical interview like CodeLive, and more. This makes hiring faster, convenient, and gives experts more time to take tests and solve problems.

Global tech hiring teams at Tesla, Unity, and Slack use Codility to screen prospects remotely, host virtual interviews with shared editor, accelerate hiring time by finding the top candidates much faster, reduce bias, increase objectivity supporting diversity, and deliver high-quality insights to hiring managers.

Pros

- Take-home coding assessments to measure every potential skill accurately and objectively while delivering stupendous candidate experience.

- Create maximum impact at leading events using online coding competitions that drive excitement.

- Develop relationships with some of the best candidates by taking by remotely interviewing them in a shared code editor.

- Accurate, easily accessible, and fair coding tests with structured interviews can mitigate unconscious bias, thus making hiring managers confident of a fair and equal process.

- Efficient insights and workflows cut down false positives and minimize interview time per hire to ensure 2.5 times faster time-to-capacity.

Codility has an assessment engine that helps recruiters select the right candidates based on their technical skills. This is the apt tool to conduct remote coding sessions with candidates.

11. HackerEarth

Founded: 2012

G2 rating: 4.5/5 Stars (316 reviews)

HackerEarth is an advanced coding assessment tool with more than 13,000 questions across 80+ skills and 63+ programming languages. The platform allows hiring managers and recruiters to create accurate coding assessments.

Pros

- Pre-configured tests for companies to use as assessments

- Multiple coding language tests

- Customizable content to suit the goal of the recruitment team

- Comprehensive reports, programmers can access lessons and different challenges through this platform

It ensures seamless integration with ATS and assists companies to screen, interview, upskill, and engage developers.

12. Pymetrics

Founded: 2011

G2 rating: 3.5/5 Stars (5 reviews)

Pymetrics is an innovative HRMS (Human Resource Management Solution) that assists businesses in streamlining the recruitment process. Using AI and behavioral analytics, this platform allows professionals to run video interviews and gamified assessments for candidates and suggest alternative roles to the ones rejected.

Pros

- Pymetrics enables enterprises to develop games complaint with ADEA (Age Discrimination in Employment Act) and modify versions for applicant with learning disabilities, ADHD, or color blindness

- HR professionals can assess existing employees by defining benchmarks for job roles

- AI-audit tools allow managers to measure and remove biases and discriminatory patterns in a performance analysis

- Pymetrics widget can be embedded into the business website and accessed through SAML

Overall, it is a soft skills platform that redefines talent management and hiring using data-driven behavioral insights.

13. Test Dome

Founded: 2013

G2 rating: 4.1/5 Stars (108 reviews)

TestDome provides work skill tests to help recruiters hire the most suitable candidates for a role faster. The tests support an array of industries such as accounting, programming, project management, customer service, and more.

Pros

- 1000+ questions to test problem solving skills in real-time

- Customize ready-to-use tests to add new and relevant questions

- Compare candidates to check their answers and results to make an insightful decision

- Prevent cheating through duplicate mail detection, webcam monitoring, and copy-paste protection

- Add multiple candidates to the existing account for free

Kand is a relatively new online assessment platform designed to help recruiters hire the best candidate. It is a pre-employment strategic tool to evaluate technological knowledge of partners, candidates, suppliers, and third-parties.

Pros

- Kand allows unbiased pre-screening, which is a valuable source of information to make better decisions

- Choose from a catalog of tech tests and use them singly or in combination with other skills

- Industry standard reports to give you robust data for improved decision making

- Behavioral analytics reports to track candidate’s movements

DevSkiller is the industry leaders offering technical screening solutions. Powered by RealLifeTesting technique, it assesses technical skills of candidates with sharp precision and provides brilliant candidate experience. As the test scores are added in the talent pipeline, recruiters can track candidate performance throughout the journey.

Pros

- 200+ tech skill tests with 5000 ready-to-use recruitment tasks

- Easily integrates with ATS

- Fully customizable and screens remotely

- Removes biases completely

## FAQs

What is pre-employment testing software?

Pre employment testing software is an advanced tool to assist hiring managers and recruiters to identify the best-fit candidates from a pool of talent.

These solutions can quickly screen candidates by assessing and identifying qualified talent, integrating with ATS, and offering multiple testing options like personality, work, job skills, aptitude, cognitive abilities, behavioral skill, and more

Why use pre-employment testing software?

Pre employment software helps recruiters assess candidates based on job-specific skills. It is an advanced tool that increases accuracy, reduces costs, and speeds up the hiring process.

How to select the best pre-employment testing software?

As the market is inundated with tools and software to assist recruiters, ask the following questions to choose the best pre-employment testing software:

- Does the software allow customization?

- Does it feature multiple pre-employment testing techniques?

- Does it offer simulators for real-world skills test?

- Does it offer online proctoring?

- Does it have 24X7 customer support?

By examining these options, you can make an informed decision to optimize your workforce's potential. Table of contents 1. iMocha 2. Cornerstone OnDemand 3. Handshake 4. Lightcast 5. Udemy Business 6. iSpring Learn 7. Skillsoft 8. Coursera for Business 9. Skillable 10. Learning Tree 11. Udacity ## Top 10 Pluralsight Alternatives & Strategic Competitors 1. iMocha iMocha is a comprehensive Pluralsight alternative designed for organizations seeking data-driven skill development and strategic workforce transformation. Its AI-powered Skills Intelligence platform bridges the gap between role requirements and employee capabilities, empowering smarter hiring, targeted upskilling, and agile internal mobility. Here’s a breakdown of its features: - Customizable Role-Based Assessments: Access 10,000+ prebuilt and custom assessments tailored to job roles, project demands, and future skill needs validating readiness before allocating learning budgets. - Skills Gap Analysis: Leverage AI-driven insights to identify workforce strengths and weaknesses, enabling precise planning for development initiatives. - Upskilling Recommendations: Based on assessment results and skill gap data, iMocha suggests targeted learning paths that align individual growth with organizational strategy. - Internal Mobility & Career Pathing: enables organizations to identify hidden talent, align employees with internal opportunities, and build personalized career paths using real-time skills data. - Learning Platform Integrations: Seamlessly connect with Coursera, Udemy, UpGrad, and Simplilearn to deliver curated training experiences at scale. G2 Rating: 4.4/5 (276 reviews) Pricing: Visit iMocha's pricing page for more details. Having trouble matching project needs with available talent? Try iMocha's Skills Intelligence Cloud. Book a demo 2. Cornerstone OnDemand Cornerstone On Demand is a talent management software company that offers a cloud-based Learning Management System (LMS) called Cornerstone Learning. With Cornerstone LMS, you can boost productivity with version management and seamless inline content workflows. Here’s a breakdown of its features: - Learning Management: It provides a platform for delivering and managing employee training programs, including features for course creation, assignment, tracking, and reporting. - On-demand access: Learners can access learning materials anytime, anywhere from any device with an internet connection. - Compliance Management: The system helps organizations ensure regulatory compliance by managing and tracking required training for employees. - Extended Enterprise: Cornerstone LMS can also be used to train external audiences like partners, vendors, and customers. G2 Rating: 4.1/5 (513 reviews) 3. Handshake Handshake is primarily focused on connecting early career talent with employers and educational opportunities. While it serves a different primary function than Pluralsight, it offers features that can complement or serve as an alternative in certain aspects. Here’s a breakdown of its features: - University Partnerships: Connects with over 1,400 colleges and universities to access a wide pool of early career talent. - Skill-Based Matching: Uses AI to match students and recent graduates with job opportunities based on their skills and interests. - Virtual Career Fairs: Facilitates online recruitment events, allowing employers to engage with candidates efficiently. - Candidate Insights: Provides detailed profiles of potential hires, including their skills, experiences, and career goals. - Career Development Resources: Provides learning materials and guidance for students and recent graduates to enhance their skills. G2 Rating: 4.5/5 (73 reviews) 4. Lightcast Lightcast (formerly EMSI Burning Glass) is a comprehensive labor market analytics platform that provides data-driven insights for workforce development and talent management. Here’s a breakdown of its features: - Real-Time Labor Market Data: Offers up-to-date information on job market trends, skill demands, and industry shifts. - Skills Taxonomy: Maintains a vast, regularly updated database of skills across industries and job roles. - Career Pathing Tools: Helps employees and organizations map out potential career trajectories based on skills and market demand. - Curriculum Analysis: Assists in aligning learning content with current and future skill needs in the job market. - Workforce Planning: Provides data-driven insights for strategic workforce planning and development. - Custom Reports and Visualizations: Creates tailored reports and interactive dashboards for easy data interpretation. G2 Rating: 4.6/5 (30 reviews) Seeking ways to make data-driven decisions about workforce planning? iMocha's Skills Intelligence Cloud can help. Book a demo 5. Udemy Business Udemy Business is a corporate learning solution that offers a vast library of courses across various professional skills. Here’s a breakdown of its features: - Extensive Course Catalog: Provides access to over 19,000 courses covering business, tech, and soft skills. - Personalized Learning Paths: Creates custom learning experiences based on individual and organizational needs. - Mobile Learning: Allows employees to access courses on-the-go through mobile apps. - Analytics and Reporting: Provides detailed insights into learner progress and course effectiveness. - Instructor-led Training: Offers options for live, virtual training sessions led by industry experts. G2 Rating: 4.5/5 (662 reviews) 6. iSpring Learn iSpring Learn is a versatile learning management system that combines course authoring tools with a robust LMS platform. Here’s a breakdown of its features: - Intuitive Course Authoring: Enables easy creation of interactive e-learning content, including quizzes and simulations. - Detailed Analytics: Provides comprehensive reports on learner progress, course effectiveness, and overall training performance. - Automated Assignment: Intelligently assigns courses based on user roles, departments, or custom criteria. - Integration Capabilities: Seamlessly integrates with HR systems and other business tools. - Virtual Classroom: Supports live online training sessions with built-in webinar functionality. - Skill Tracking: Allows mapping of courses to specific skills, enabling targeted skill development. G2 Rating: 4.6/5 (111 reviews) 7. Skillsoft Skillsoft offers a wide range of learning content and talent development solutions that position it as a strong Pluralsight alternative. Here's a breakdown of its features: - Extensive Course Library: Provides a vast collection of courses covering technology, business, and leadership skills. - Percipio Learning Platform: Offers an intelligent learning experience platform with personalized content recommendations. - Compliance Training: Provides comprehensive compliance courses to meet regulatory requirements across industries. - Multi-modal Learning: Delivers content in various formats including videos, books, audiobooks, and coaching. - Skill Benchmarking: Allows organizations to assess and benchmark employees' skills against industry standards. - Integration Capabilities: Seamlessly integrates with existing LMS and HR systems for streamlined talent management. G2 Rating: 4.2/5 (96 reviews) 8. Coursera for Business Coursera for Business leverages its vast library of university and industry-partner content to provide comprehensive learning solutions for organizations. Here’s a breakdown of its features: - Curated Content Collections: Offers pre-packaged learning programs tailored to specific business needs and industry trends. - Skill Development Tracking: Measures and tracks employee skill development across various domains. - Custom Learning Paths: Allows creation of personalized learning journeys aligned with organizational goals and individual career aspirations. - Recognized Certifications: Offers professional certificates from top universities and companies, enhancing employee credentials. - Advanced Analytics: Provides detailed insights into learner engagement, progress, and skill development. G2 Rating: 4.5/5 (438 reviews) 9. Skillable Skillable is a cloud-based lab platform that focuses on providing hands-on, experiential learning for technology skills. Here’s a breakdown of its features: - Virtual Lab Environments: Offers cloud-based, sandbox environments for risk-free practice of tech skills. - Scored Labs: Automatically evaluates learners' performance in lab exercises, providing immediate feedback. - Learning Paths: Enables creation of custom learning journeys that combine theory and practical application. - Analytics and Reporting: Provides detailed insights into learner progress, skill acquisition, and areas for improvement. - API and LMS Integration: Easily integrates with existing learning management systems and other educational tools. G2 Rating: 4.6/5 (399 reviews) 10. Learning Tree Learning Tree offers a wide range of instructor-led and online training courses, focusing on IT and management skills. Here’s a breakdown of its features: - Blended Learning Approach: Offers a mix of online, in-person, and virtual instructor-led training options. - Certification Programs: Prepares learners for industry-recognized certifications in IT and project management. - Customized Corporate Training: Tailors training programs to meet specific organizational needs and objectives. - Learning Paths: Offers structured sequences of courses designed to build comprehensive skill sets in specific areas. - Adaptive Learning Platform: Provides personalized learning experiences based on individual progress and preferences. - Skills Assessment Tools: Helps identify skill gaps and recommends appropriate training courses. G2 Rating: 2.5/5 (2 reviews) 11. Udacity Udacity offers cutting-edge tech education through its "Nanodegree" programs and partnerships with leading tech companies. Here’s a breakdown of its features: - Nanodegree Programs: Provides comprehensive, project-based learning paths in emerging tech fields. - Expert Mentorship: Provides one-on-one technical mentorship and career coaching. - Flexible Learning: Allows self-paced learning to accommodate working professionals. - Career Services: Offers resume support, LinkedIn profile optimization, and interview preparation. - Enterprise Solutions: Provides customized upskilling programs for businesses. - Skills-based Approach: Focuses on practical, job-ready skills rather than theoretical knowledge. G2 Rating: 4.5/5 (758 reviews) ### Conclusion Choosing the right Pluralsight alternative takes more than just access to courses. You need a platform that supports real business results. While every tool in this list has its benefits, iMocha stands out for companies that want to build a skills-first workforce. With AI-powered assessments, skills gap analysis, career pathing, and easy integrations with learning platforms, iMocha helps teams do more than just train. It gives clear skills insights, supports smarter decisions, and helps you fill gaps, grow talent from within, and prepare for the future. Struggling to identify skill gaps in your organization? Try iMocha Skills Intelligence Cloud and get granular insights into your workforce capabilities. Book a demo ### FAQs What are the best Pluralsight alternatives? The best Pluralsight alternatives include iMocha, Cornerstone OnDemand, and Skillable. Some of these platforms offer a wide range of courses while some provide learning paths tailored to various professional and personal development needs. Why is iMocha better than Pluralsight? iMocha is better than Pluralsight for organizations focusing on comprehensive skills insights and upskilling. It’s a complete solution that helps with skills development, internal mobility, workforce planning, and targeted development. Skills assessment tools are used to evaluate candidates’ and employees’ abilities across technical, cognitive, and behavioral competencies. They play a critical role in modern hiring and workforce development by replacing subjective resume screening with data-driven insights, enabling organizations to identify job-ready talent more accurately and efficiently.

more
As skills-based hiring becomes the standard, organizations increasingly rely on methods such as coding tests, situational judgment tests, and AI-powered evaluations to measure real-world capabilities. According to the World Economic Forum’s Future of Jobs Report 2023, six in ten workers will require training before 2027, but only half currently have access to adequate training opportunities.

This highlights the growing importance of continuous skill validation in both recruitment and employee development.

## What Key Features Should You Look for in a Skills Assessment Tool?

Choosing the right skills assessment tool can improve your hiring and training process. Here are key features to look for:

- Customization Options: Ability to change tests to fit different roles and departments.

- Pre-built Test Library: Large selection of ready-made tests covering technical, thinking, and soft skills.

- AI-Based Scoring & Analytics: Clear reports showing skills and performance gaps.

- Anti-Cheating Features: Tools like video checks, copy-paste blocking, and webcam snapshots.

- Integration Capability: Easy connection with your ATS, LMS, or HR software.

- Candidate Experience: Simple interface that's easy for candidates to use.

In this listicle, we review the top 12 skills assessment tools for 2026, comparing their features and strengths to help you choose the right solution for your hiring and talent strategy.EndFragment

Table of contents

#1 iMocha

#2 TestGorilla

#3 TestDome

#4 Wonderlic

#5 eSkill

#6 Xobin

#7 Codility

#8 Mettl

#9 Vervoe

#10 CoderPad

#11 HireVue

#12 HackerRank

#13 ProProfs Quiz Maker

## Top 13 Skills Assessment Tools

1. iMocha

iMocha is a skills assessment tool that enables organizations to validate real-world skills with AI-powered precision and scalability.

It offers role-based assessments across technical, cognitive, language, and domain skills, supported by advanced proctoring and AI-driven analytics. The platform helps teams make accurate hiring and workforce decisions by identifying skill gaps and predicting performance at scale.

Key Features:

- Extensive Assessment Library: Access 10,000+ skill assessment tests covering technical, cognitive, functional, and soft skills.

- Coding Assessments: Evaluate programming skills using hands-on challenges, multiple compilers, and a wide range of coding problems.

- Tara – AI Interviewer: Conduct on-demand, conversational AI interviews with automated scoring, transcripts, and consistent candidate evaluation.

- Advanced Proctoring & Anti-Cheating: Ensure test integrity with AI-based proctoring, browser restrictions, and plagiarism detection.

- Skill Intelligence Platform: Map, benchmark, and manage workforce skills to support hiring, upskilling, and internal mobility.

- AI-Powered Skill Analytics: Gain insights into skill proficiency, gaps, and workforce readiness with data-driven reports.

Pros:

- It allows you to assess the candidate’s competency level—beginner, intermediate, proficient, and experienced efficaciously

- It provides insightful assessment reports that enable employees to see their skills, competency, areas of improvement, and training efficacy

- iMocha creates necessary APIs for seamless integration with legacy ATS, job boards, and more

Cons:

- iMocha does not conduct psychometric tests

- It does not provide background checks for candidates

Clients: Deloitte, PayPal, Fujitsu, Capgemini, Cognizant, Wipro, CGI

Pricing: Visit iMocha's pricing page for more details.

G2 Rating: 4.4/5 (276 reviews)

Boost Hiring Accuracy – Learn How Skills Assessments Can Transform Your Recruitment Process!

Start your free trial

2. TestGorilla

TestGorilla is a popular hiring assessment tool offering over 250 tests in technical skills, thinking, personality, and soft skills. It helps companies hire fairly with anti-cheating tools, webcam checks, and easy-to-share candidate reports. Good for small and large companies simplifying early-stage hiring.

Key Features:

- Pre-built Test Library: Access a wide range of assessments covering technical skills, cognitive ability, personality, and culture fit.

- Custom Test Creation: Combine multiple tests or add role-specific questions tailored to job requirements.

- Anti-Cheating Measures: Includes webcam monitoring, browser tracking, and question randomization to maintain test integrity.

- Automated Candidate Screening: Rank candidates with performance-based scorecards for faster decision-making.

- ATS Integrations: Connect with applicant tracking systems to streamline recruitment workflows.

Pros:

- It allows you to follow a candidate's recruitment funnel effortlessly.

- It offers 250+ skills assessments in critical areas such as mental aptitude, culture fit, and other fundamental abilities.

- TestGorilla balances assessment difficulty very well to finalize only deserving candidates.

Cons:

- TestGorilla's virtual customer support does not respond.

- This technical assessment tool lacks live video interviews.

Clients: Majorel, H&M, Public Groupe, Oracle, Bain & Company

Pricing: Pay-as-you-go model

G2 Rating: 4.5/5 (1023 reviews)

Here’s why enterprises prefer iMocha over TestGorilla

3. TestDome

TestDome is an affordable skills test tool for small and medium-sized businesses. It provides tests in programming, finance, and customer service roles. It has a simple interface and regularly updated test content, making it a good choice for companies wanting up-to-date assessments.

Key Features:

- Pre-built Test Library: Access role-based assessments across programming, finance, customer service, and other job functions.

- Custom Test Creation: Combine or customize tests with role-specific questions to match hiring requirements.

- Automated Scoring: Evaluate candidate responses instantly with system-generated scores for faster decision-making.

- Real-World Assessments: Use scenario-based questions to assess practical skills and job readiness.

- User-Friendly Interface: Provide a simple and intuitive experience for both recruiters and candidates.

Pros:

- TestDome is priced conveniently for smaller companies

- The platform is highly user-friendly

- Its skills are constantly updated to include new ones to keep up with the market trends.

Cons:

- TestDome does not allow candidates to customize templates, logos, design invites, or integration.

- The platform does not allow you to change assessment timings.

- It offers limited assessments available for data science.

Clients: McAfee, indeed, EY, Adobe, UNICEF, PayPal

Pricing: $20/month (per user)

G2 Rating: 4.5/5 (108 reviews)

4. Wonderlic

Wonderlic provides tests in thinking ability, personality, and motivation, mostly for frontline roles. Often used by staffing agencies, Wonderlic helps recruiters find the right fit using behavioral science and simple data analysis.

Key Features:

- Cognitive Ability Testing: Evaluate problem-solving, learning ability, and decision-making skills.

- Personality Assessments: Measure behavioral traits, motivation, and workplace preferences.

- Standardized Scoring: Generate reliable and validated scores for consistent candidate evaluation.

- Behavioral Insights: Gain insights into candidate fit for specific roles and work environments.

- High-Volume Hiring Support: Assess large candidate pools efficiently for frontline and entry-level roles.

Pros of Wonderlic:

- The tool best suits businesses or recruitment service providers (RPOs) with a high volume of recruitment work in front-line positions such as retail, sales, customer service, contact centers, airline, and graduate positions.

- It provides a cognitive, motivation, and personality rating that can be critical for employers during the live interview process.

- It has a user-friendly UI/UX.

Cons of Wonderlic:

- Wonderlic does not provide any customer support service.

- This tool’s assessments are lengthy and time-consuming.

Clients: Aveda, Duracell, Subway, Sedgwick County, Champion Auto

Pricing: Not mentioned publicly.

G2 Rating: 4.3/5 (124 reviews)

Looking to create a skills bar to ensure quality while hiring? Use iMocha's skills assessment to hire skill-fit candidates.

Start your free trial

5. eSkill

eSkill has many tests covering technical, administrative, and customer service skills. HR teams can copy and edit existing tests or easily build their own using a drag-and-drop tool. Often used in education, government, and healthcare.

Key Features:

- Assessment Library: Access a wide range of skill assessments across technical, administrative, and customer service roles.

- Custom Test Creation: Create or customize tests using a drag-and-drop interface to match job requirements.

- Simulation-Based Assessments: Use real-world scenarios to evaluate job-specific skills.

- Automated Scoring: Generate instant results and detailed reports for faster candidate evaluation.

- Job-Based Assessments: Assess candidates based on specific roles, industries, and functional skills.

Pros:

- It's easy to create a test using eSkill's pre-loaded questions. Users can also duplicate and customize a test based on the job role to make it more relevant to the job requisition.

- There is an impressive level of detail in their pre-made exams, which cover everything from general skills to job roles.

- eSkill has an extensive library of market and industry-specific evaluations, making it one of the well-recognized soft skills assessment tools.

Cons:

- eSkill does not allow test model payment. Each year, you must purchase the entire model, which is more than you need.

- It has a complicated UI, making it hard to explore the platform.

Clients: Coca-Cola, Work Personnel, State of Colorado, Emory University, Pandora

Pricing: Not mentioned publicly.

G2 Rating: 4.5/5 (329 reviews)

6. Xobin

Xobin is a skills assessment tool that helps organizations evaluate candidates across technical, cognitive, and role-based skills. It supports efficient hiring through AI-driven assessments, automated evaluation, and secure testing environments. The platform is commonly used for screening candidates at scale and improving hiring accuracy.

Key Features:

- Skill Assessment Library: Access a wide range of assessments across technical, cognitive, and role-specific skills.

- AI-Based Evaluation: Analyze candidate performance with automated scoring and detailed insights.

- Coding Assessments: Evaluate programming skills using real-world coding challenges across multiple technologies.

- Proctoring & Anti-Cheating: Ensure test integrity with features like browser monitoring and plagiarism detection.

- Custom Test Creation: Create or customize assessments tailored to specific job roles and hiring needs.

Pros: StartFragment

- Supports assessments across technical, cognitive, and role-specific skills.

- Provides automated scoring with AI-driven evaluation for faster decision-making.

- Offers coding assessments with real-world challenges across multiple technologies.

Cons: StartFragment

- Limited advanced analytics compared to enterprise-level platforms.

- Interface may require a learning curve for new users.

- Customization options may be limited for highly specialized roles.

Clients: Reliance, DELL, Sharpminds, randstad

Pricing: Starting from $699/year

G2 Rating: 4.7/5 (232 reviews)

Meet iMocha, the DevSkiller alternative!

7. Codility

Codility lets recruiters test developers using automated coding tests. Users can make custom tests, get real-time feedback, and hire across many tech skills. It has a clear interface and good reporting, ideal for hiring growing engineering teams.

Key Features:

- Coding Assessments: Evaluate developer skills using coding tests across multiple programming languages.

- Live Technical Interviews: Conduct real-time coding interviews in a collaborative environment.

- Automated Code Evaluation: Analyze code for correctness, efficiency, and scalability with instant results.

- Developer Testing Environment: Provide an intuitive interface designed for technical assessments.

- Scalable Hiring Workflows: Manage large-scale developer hiring with structured evaluation processes.

Pros:

- The platform is made with such ease that HR professionals, who typically don’t know how to code, can also deploy assessments quickly. They can assess applicants' skills against other programmers without additional technical help

- Codility helps you create a collection of code tasks suitable for specific job types

- To ensure that customers' concerns are being addressed, Codility's account manager conducts monthly follow-ups

Cons:

- Codility has no debug pane (a tool to fix all software errors), which makes testing more difficult for users

- Users can easily copy and paste answers from other web pages since it doesn’t provide anti-cheating features, such as video monitoring or image proctoring

Clients: Unity, Zalando, Paypal, American Express, Intel

Pricing: Not mentioned publicly.

G2 Rating: 4.6 /5 (408 reviews)

8. Mettl

Mercer Mettl provides tests in skills and personality with detailed data analytics and secure testing. It is good for large companies needing security and flexibility. With coding and behavioral tests, it works well for hiring and employee training at big companies.

Key Features:

- Assessment Library: Access a wide range of assessments across technical, cognitive, and behavioral skills.

- Custom Test Creation: Create or customize assessments to match specific job roles and hiring needs.

- Advanced Proctoring: Ensure secure and credible assessments with AI-based monitoring and controls.

- Detailed Analytics: Generate in-depth reports and insights for data-driven decision-making.

- Enterprise Assessment Solutions: Support large-scale hiring and workforce development with flexible assessment frameworks.

Pros:

- Assessments are divided into many modules, allowing applicants to choose individual modules or combine different modules to meet their needs

- Mettl provides users graphs and subjective data that help them understand the level of their skills

Cons:

- Mettl does not provide an AVG Score or excel reports (local or global standard)

- It has a complex U.I., hindering users' experience

Clients: Ghent University Global Campus, MakeMyTrip, Workforce, Gulf University, NASSCOM

Pricing: $249/year

G2 Rating: 4.4/5 (499 reviews)

Worried about lengthy candidate screening process? Reduce hiring time by 40% with iMocha's skills assessments

Start your free trial

9. Vervoe

Vervoe provides interactive tests for roles like sales, customer service, and marketing. It lets companies use video, audio, text, and coding answers scored by AI. Good for companies wanting realistic job skill tests and high candidate involvement.

Key Features:

- AI-Powered Skill Assessments: Evaluate candidates using AI-scored tests across sales, customer service, marketing, and more.

- Simulation-Based Testing: Assess real-world job performance through task-based and scenario-driven questions.

- Multi-Format Responses: Collect answers in video, audio, text, and coding formats for deeper evaluation.

- Automated Candidate Ranking: Rank candidates based on performance using AI-driven scoring and insights.

- Custom Assessment Creation: Build and customize assessments tailored to specific roles and job requirements.

Pros:

- With everything in one place, the Vervoe application and screening process are quick and easy

- Vervoe allows you to customize your assessments using a variety of question types — multiple choice, essay, video, audio, visual, etc.

- It features 10+ immersive question categories, such as ones that require video responses and coding

Cons:

- The pricing model is arbitrary and not flexible

- The software is not mobile-friendly

- They have poor customer service

Clients: Myob, TriNet, Australia Post, WPP, OmnicomGroup, K-FORCE

G2 Rating: 4.6/5 (64 reviews)

Pricing: $149/month

10. CoderPad

CoderPad is a developer-focused testing tool supporting over 30 programming languages. It lets companies do live coding interviews in real-time. Popular with tech companies for hiring engineers by testing them on real project tasks in a shared coding environment.

Key Features:

- Live Coding Interviews: Conduct real-time coding interviews in a shared environment with instant collaboration.

- Multi-Language Support: Evaluate candidates across a wide range of programming languages and frameworks.

- Real-World Coding Environment: Provide an IDE-like interface that simulates actual development workflows.

- Code Execution & Testing: Run and test code instantly during interviews to assess correctness and approach.

### FAQs

1. What is a skills assessment tool?

A skills assessment tool is used to evaluate candidates’ and employees’ abilities across technical, cognitive, and behavioral skills using structured tests and real-world scenarios.

2. What are the benefits of using skills assessment software?

Skills assessment software helps improve hiring accuracy, reduce bias, identify skill gaps, and enable data-driven decisions for both recruitment and employee development.

3. What are skill assessment tests?

Skill assessment tests are structured evaluations that measure a candidate’s proficiency in specific skills such as coding, communication, problem-solving, or job-related tasks.

4. What types of skills can be assessed?

Skills assessment tools can evaluate technical skills, cognitive abilities, soft skills, language proficiency, and role-specific competencies.

5. How do I ensure candidate privacy and data security?

Choose tools with enterprise-grade security certifications (SOC 2, ISO 27001), clear data retention policies, and compliance with relevant privacy regulations (GDPR, CCPA).

6. What if candidates find assessments too difficult or time-consuming?

Look for tools offering customizable difficulty levels, reasonable time limits, and mobile-friendly interfaces. Consider providing clear expectations and practice opportunities to improve candidate experience.

Talent management assessment tools evaluate workforce capabilities against job requirements and organizational goals to identify skill gaps. These insights help organizations create targeted learning, upskilling, and workforce development programs. 3. What should organizations look for in a talent management assessment tool? Organizations should consider assessment capabilities, skills intelligence features, workforce analytics, succession planning support, integration options, scalability, and assessment validity when selecting a talent management assessment tool. 4. How often should organizations conduct talent management assessments? Organizations typically conduct talent management assessments annually or biannually to evaluate workforce capabilities and development needs. Using recruitment analytics, you can ascertain the practices that work, the ones that don’t, candidates’ preferences, their motivations, the skills level at your organization benchmarked with the industry level, and more.

### Why is recruitment analytics important?

Recruitment analytics is important because it helps organizations understand where they are losing potential candidates, their hiring funnel, and what sources are providing the most qualified candidates. Additionally, recruitment analytics can help organizations make better, data-driven choices.

### What are the sources of data for recruitment channel analytics?

There are a few common data sources for recruitment analytics. This data can come from a variety of sources, such as:

- Pre-employment Testing Analytics

- Applicant Tracking System (ATS)

- Customer Relationship Management (CRM)

- Human Resources Information System (HRIS)

- Candidate Surveys

If you’re thinking…. did she really ask me if I have heard what a chain reaction was? Then yes, I did! more I know it is a blog about recruiters and candidates, but really, do you know WHAT IS A CHAIN REACTION? Well, if you don’t, here’s what it means- “A chain reaction is a sequence of reactions where a reactive product or by-product causes additional reactions to take place.” - Wikipedia To help you understand how is it related to the candidate experience. Here’s a story- “I once had an interview scheduled at 10.A.M in the morning. I reached there and to my surprise, there wasn’t anyone present to greet me. The recruiter herself was running late, and I was told “she’ll reach the office within 20mins”. However, I was there till 12.30 P.M but the recruiter didn’t show up. Then, two senior employees with very little knowledge about my work domain decided to take my interview. Finally, I left the building at 1.30 P.M without meeting the recruiter. Even though I really needed a job at that point in time, I had made up my mind not to settle for it. They called me again, and without an apology, I was asked to submit an assignment. This is was the last nail in the coffin and I decided not to associate with them.” Now, do you think I would recommend them to others? You are right, no! I won’t and this is the chain reaction i.e., the company’s overall branding will be hampered wherever I go, and from there so on and so forth. This is exactly what happens when you, as a recruiter, don’t take efforts to enhance the overall candidate experience. ## What Is Candidate Experience? Candidate experience is all about respecting the candidates as well as their time. How do you treat them when they come to your office, regardless of whether they are selected or not? If you have told them “we’ll get back to you” then give them a call with feedback within a stipulated amount of time. Be prompt towards the candidate and lastly, not treating anyone as an option! ## When Does Candidate Experience Begins? It starts at the same moment when you post a job opportunity on your preferred recruitment platform. It goes till the technical screening process and even extends till you and the candidate decide to part ways. However, caring about candidate experience is not all about the cool merchandise or gifts you give to the candidate. It can certainly be termed as a part of it). But, candidate experience is all about how the organization treats the candidate right from the first point of contact till the end of the process. How long do you make the candidate wait, how many times you do or do not reschedule the interviews, and so on. Trust me, those merchandise that you hand over to the candidate as a thank you gift won’t change the opinion about the organization. Also Read: 11 Steps Towards Transforming Assessment And Candidate Experience ## Why Does Candidate Experience Matter And Who’s Responsible? When you post a job requirement, it reaches an unlimited number of people all across the internet. The number of people you connect with, over a job description is 10x more than what it would be 10 years back. Now, think about all the candidates you’ve interacted with to fill different jobs in the last year. The way you respond to them, coordinate with them and eventually finalize the entire process of interviewing/hiring with them, creates an image of your organization in their head. If you carry out the entire process right, no matter whether the candidate is selected or not, they become the promoters of your company. They would be more than willing to share their experience with their professional connections. And, that’s exactly what you are looking for! Now, the question arises…. ## Who’s Responsible For Candidate Experience? Like us, Bullhorn was also keen to know the responsibility factor when it came to candidate experience. Therefore, the result was 48% said it is the individual recruiter's responsibility. However, 45% said it is a shared responsibility i.e., recruiters and the whole organization. I can’t agree more with the latter 45%. I know since the recruiter is in the front lines with the candidates, they are more accountable. But, that doesn’t mean they are fully responsible. However, it isn’t hard to understand that improving the candidate experience is a team effort. Little things like how welcoming and helpful the other employees of the company are, also play a major role in building a good candidate experience. Here’s something we can learn from the consumer industries. They are way ahead of the game when it comes to enhancing the customer experience. They have consumer feedback portals and they want the customer to experience the least amount of inconvenience. A recruiter can introduce similar metrics in the organization to measure the candidate experience and how they can improve it. However, when such an organization-wide feedback method is introduced, the responsibility doesn’t only rely on the shoulders of the recruiter. It is everyone’s responsibility. What are your opinions on candidate experience? Does the candidate experience matter in your recruitment strategy? When do you think organizations will start taking candidate feedback? # What is a Pre-Employment Assessment Test?

Table of contents
Text Link

Want to hire individuals immediately, but finding it extremely difficult?

Well, hiring is undoubtedly a daunting task. Plus, the urgency of filling the position with the right candidates makes it more challenging.

That is why having a pre-employment assessment is a must-have today. It can transform your talent pipeline. Enhance the hiring experience for both employers and employees.

By using employment tests recruiters can identify suitable candidates for a job while minimizing the risk of making the wrong hire, which can be costly and time-consuming. These assessments are designed to evaluate a candidate's skills, abilities and personality traits providing insights that aid employers in making hiring decisions.

In this article we'll delve into what pre-employment assessment test is, why they matter to both employers and job seekers and explore types of tests available in today's market.

Let's jump right in.

## What is a Pre-Employment Assessment Test?

A pre-employment assessment test is essentially a pre-employment testing software that employers use to assess the skills, capabilities, personality traits and other pertinent qualities of job applicants.

Being one of the essential candidate screening method, assessments help ascertain whether an applicant aligns well with both the job requirements and the company's culture.

Keep in mind that pre-employment evaluations can come in formats, such as tests, skills assessments, personality evaluations and behavioral interviews.

Are you concerned that lengthy screening processes are impacting candidate experience? Check out how iMocha can help you reduce your hiring time by 40%!
Book a demo

## Types of Pre-employment Assessment Tests

### 1. Cognitive Ability Tests

Cognitive assessments are used to assess an applicant's problem-solving skills, ability to learn information and logical reasoning. Recruiters utilize these tests to evaluate a candidate's capabilities and gauge their potential for success in a specific role.

In other words, these assessments are highly effective in evaluating an individual's abilities encompassing their aptitude for problem-solving, thinking and proficiency in verbal and numerical reasoning.

Such assessments often cover topics like mathematics, logic and language comprehension.

Here is a list of 88+ cognitive pre-employment tests to help you assess your talent’s cognitive abilities.

### 2. Personality Tests

Personality assessments are used to gauge an applicant's disposition and qualities such as stability, conscientiousness and extroversion.

These evaluations are specifically designed to measure an individual's personality traits and characteristics.

They assist employers in evaluating the following;

- How well an individual will integrate into the company culture.

- How they will engage with colleagues and customers.

Some of the recognized examples of personality assessments include the Myers Briggs Type Indicator (MBTI) the assessment of Big Five personality traits and the Hogan Personality Inventory.

(Image source)

### 3. Cultural Fitment Test

Cultural fit assessments typically involve comparing a candidate's preferences for culture with the actual culture of the company they are applying to. This allows companies to gain insight into how an applicant's values align with the values of the organization.

Candidates who demonstrate cultural fitness contribute to creating a positive work environment fostering effective teamwork and enhancing employee engagement.

### 4. Soft Skills Test

Soft skills refer to the technical abilities required to excel in a job, such as effective communication, problem solving capabilities, teamwork and integrity.

When evaluating candidates, for a position recruiters can focus on assessing individuals who possess the skills particularly if the specific tasks associated with the job can be acquired through learning and experience.$

/$

### 5. Job Knowledge Tests

These assessments are created to evaluate a person's expertise in an area or industry. They assist employers in gauging an individual's grasp of concepts, principles and practices that's relevant to the job position.

Some instances of knowledge tests for jobs include the National Council Licensure Examination (NCLEX), for nursing professionals the Project Management Professional (PMP) exam and the Certified Public Accountant (CPA) exam.

### 6. Skills Tests

There are various types of skills tests that help assess an individual's specific skills in a particular area or field.

More specifically, they help evaluate an applicant's proficiency in specific job-related skills, such as typing, coding, or writing. They can help employers evaluate an individual's proficiency in tasks that are critical for a particular job role.

Platforms like iMocha offer a variety of pre-employment tests in areas such as coding, digital marketing, and software testing. Here are some of the platform's most unique and recruiter-friendly features:

- AI-LogicBox

AI LogicBox functions, as 'Code in the Blanks' offering an intelligent approach to coding compared to traditional coding assessments. It prioritizes implementation and creativity, over syntax.

By utilizing intelligence, it evaluates the problem-solving skills and critical thinking abilities of individuals taking the test.

The AI LogicBox presents scenarios. Challenges that necessitate the test takers demonstration of logical reasoning to solve problems.

- Live Coding

The Live Coding interview feature is designed to assess the coding skills of test-takers in real time:

It allows recruiters to evaluate a candidate's coding abilities by presenting them with coding challenges that they must solve within a set time limit. The Live Coding feature supports several programming languages and frameworks.

## Benefits of Pre-employment Assessment Tests

### 1. Helps Predict Job Performance

One of the benefits of incorporating pre-employment assessment tests is their ability to gauge the skills, knowledge and abilities of candidates which are crucial for achieving success in a job.

By assessing candidates using these criteria employers can make predictions about their job performance.

### 2. Provides a Standardized Evaluation Process

Pre-employment assessment tests offer an evaluation procedure that ensures all candidates are assessed consistently and fairly. This enables employers to make hiring decisions that are more objective and well-informed.

### 3. Reduces Hiring Bias

Pre-employment assessment tests are valuable in addressing hiring bias as they offer data supporting insights into a candidate's skills and qualifications. This enables employers to make fairer hiring choices while minimizing the influence of bias.

### 4. Saves Time and Money in the Hiring Process

It can also contribute to streamlining the hiring process by offering an effective means of evaluating candidates. Through the utilization of these tests, employers can save time and resources that would otherwise be expended on hiring procedures and less productive interviews.

A pre-employment assessment test is essentially a pre-employment assessment tool that employers use to assess the skills, capabilities, personality traits and other pertinent qualities of job applicants.

## How Pre-Employment Assessment Tests Are Administered

Recruiters can administer pre-employment tests in three ways:

### A. Online Assessments

Nowadays online platforms are commonly used to administer pre-employment assessment tests. These tests can be accessed with an internet connection. Provide flexibility for candidates to complete them at their own convenience whether timed or untimed.

### B. In-Person Assessments

Some companies prefer to conduct pre-employment assessment tests, in person during the interview phase. These assessments can include activities, like role-playing, simulations or other exercises meant to assess a candidate's skills and abilities.

### C. Proctored Assessments

Proctored pre-employment assessment tests are typically conducted under supervision in a controlled environment such as a testing center.

These assessments are commonly employed for positions or roles that involve stakes or require security and confidentiality measures.

## In Conclusion

To sum up, pre-employment assessment tests are tests specifically designed to evaluate a candidate's job-related skills, cognitive abilities and personality traits.

They offer advantages to organizations;

- They empower employers to make hiring decisions and minimize the risk of hiring individuals who are not suitable for the job or the organization.

- These tests enhance hiring accuracy by providing standardized data that can predict a candidate's job performance.

- By reducing the number of candidates that need to be screened and interviewed they save time and money.

Overall pre-employment assessment tests provide insights for employers throughout the hiring process.

## FAQs

### 1. What is the purpose of the pre-employment assessment?

Pre-employment evaluations are utilized to assess a job applicant's abilities, character and other attributes in order to ascertain their suitability for a job or organization.

The aim of these evaluations is to furnish employers with information that aids in making informed hiring choices and mitigating the chances of selecting an unsuitable candidate.

### 2. What is the difference between an assessment and an interview?

Assessments involve using tests or questionnaires to collect information about a candidate's skills and traits whereas interviews are subjective and rely on conversations between the interviewer and the candidate.

While interviews provide employers with in-depth insights into a candidate's experience and qualifications they can be affected by factors like bias and the candidate's performance under pressure.

### 3. What are the pros and cons of pre-employment assessments?

There are advantages, to using employment assessments;

- Objectivity

- Validity

- Efficiency

On the hand there are also some drawbacks associated with employment assessments;

- Potential for Bias

- Potential for Cheating

Technical skills assessments are transforming hiring, enabling recruiters to evaluate candidates efficiently. 75% of recruiters expect skill-based hiring to dominate within 18 months.

By leveraging data-backed assessments, organizations can make informed hiring decisions while reducing time-to-hire.

Screening or assessment tools go beyond filtering resumes. They provide an objective measure of a candidate’s job readiness. By integrating these tools, organizations can improve hiring efficiency and reduce bias in candidate evaluations.

# DevOps Hiring Best Practices for DevOps Team Setup

Table of contents
Text Link

Recently DevOps mythology has gained massive popularity amongst many companies, mainly because of its ability to push higher quality software, faster delivery times, and ultimately, safer systems.

Implementing DevOps as a stand-alone technique is challenging. As a result, as substantiated in the image below, enterprises are increasingly developing DevOps adoption approaches that align with business goals.

(source)

In fact, a recent study conducted by Global Market Insights reveals that the industry's future shows encouraging numbers. In 2019 the size of the DevOps market exceeded $4 billion and was projected to grow at a CAGR of over 20% between 2020 and 2026.

However, hiring DevOps engineers can be a daunting task. It requires recruiters to be aware of all the ideal platforms for sourcing talented candidates, technical and non-technical skills, and more.

In this article, we have outlined some DevOps hiring best practices that you can utilize to hire skilled DevOps engineers.

So, let's dive deep!

## Best Practices for selecting the right DevOps Candidates

### 1. Hire based on the specific need

Outlining the specific need of the position is the first and foremost approach you can take to select the right DevOps candidates.

If you are planning to build a DevOps team from scratch, you need to identify the structure followed within your organization. Pinpoint the areas which need immediate need. It will enable you to identify what gaps you are required to fulfill and what to expect from the candidate while hiring.

But, if you currently have a DevOps team and are searching for a specific person, you are likely well aware of the fact that most DevOps professionals bring a variety of abilities to the table. That's where you can easily identify if you are looking for design, implementation, security, testing, deployment, management, or some combination of knowledge.

### 2. Develop a clear job description$

/$

You get a highly specialized group of professionals when you design your DevOps team from the bottom up. It is, therefore, advisable to provide thorough job descriptions that include the skills and expertise needed for the position.

While creating the DevOps job description, clearly mention the following:

- Expectations for the role and what the DevOps Engineer will be responsible for.

- Technical skills, experience, and qualifications necessary to be successful in the role.

- List the specific tasks, duties, and responsibilities that the DevOps Engineer will have.

- Describe the tools the DevOps Engineer will need to be familiar with and use.

- Explain the communication requirements of the role and how the DevOps Engineer will interact with other teams.

- Describe how the DevOps Engineer will collaborate with other teams in the organization.

- Explain how the DevOps Engineer will report their progress and results.

- Provide any other information that is relevant to the role.

Accelerate Your DevOps Hiring! With iMocha, create tailored skills assessments to identify top talent efficiently. Cut your hiring time in half and ensure a perfect fit for your niche DevOps roles.
Start your free trial

### 3. Build Employment database

Another DevOps hiring best practice is building an employee pipeline. It helps you get in touch with talented DevOps candidates. Since the DevOps field is in high demand, finding a high-skill DevOps Engineer immediately is challenging.

Thus, many of the best candidates are currently employed and may never see your job advertising unless you reach out to them directly.

So, how can you reach out to them?

Well, utilize a combination of online and offline networking to potential source candidates. LinkedIn and Monster, Indeed, network groups, and other similar locations can be great places to start.

Another method is to leverage referral programs. People in similar professions often network with one another, and employee referrals can be an excellent way to gather new candidates.

### 4. Take help with sourcing tools

The DevOps hiring process is undoubtedly challenging. As it can be tough to find the ideal DevOps candidates, there are many sourcing tools available in the market to help you streamline the recruitment process.

These tools enable you to find and recruit the best candidates by searching for candidates on various job boards and social media platforms.

It also tracks and monitors the progress of applications, creates job postings, shares job postings across multiple channels, and more. Here is a list of 12 sourcing tools you can utilize to make your DevOps recruiting journey more seamless.

### 5. Don't settle with local talent

Technology has enabled people to work and manage their work from any location. Moreover, many employees are seeking for flexible work culture due to the increasing adaptation of work from home and hybrid work culture.

Thus, you can hire local talent or consider people from other locations while conducting DevOps recruiting. Many skilled DevOps engineers around the world are seeking job opportunities. And the chances of filing for a job position using flexible work culture are much ease.

## Best Practices for Assessing DevOps Engineer Skills

(source)

### 6. Assess the technical abilities of candidates

DevOps engineers have specific skills and abilities they need to train; if they aren't what you're looking for, you will be disappointed in who you find. Thus, assessing technical skills is one of the DevOps hiring best practices.

But what technical skills to look for when hiring a DevOps engineer?

- Knowledge of tools like Docker, Amazon, Bamboo, Puppet, Jenkins, and Kubernetes.

- Understanding Linux/Unix fundamentals and programming languages like Python, Ruby, and Perl.

- Knowledge of IT security

- Strong knowledge of the most recent methods and technologies for delivering applications, such as Amazon, Azure, and Google Compute Engine (GCE).

- Automate the release management process by coordinating software releases.

- Incorporating agile development approaches into the company's best practices for creating new products and improving current ones.

# How to Assess & Hire Programmers in 2026

Table of contents
Text Link

Hiring programmers can feel challenging when you are not from a technical background. It can be difficult to judge the depth of a candidate’s coding knowledge. It can also be confusing to evaluate technical jargon or verify what a developer claims during interviews.

The good news is that you do not need to be a programmer to hire a great one. With a structured hiring process and the right tools, you can confidently evaluate technical talent and choose a candidate who is capable, reliable, and a strong cultural fit.

This guide will walk you through a clear and practical process that any HR or non technical recruiter can use to hire programmers with confidence.

## Why a Assessment Test Should Be Your First Step

Before you begin shortlisting candidates through resumes, start with an aptitude or skills assessment test. A resume alone cannot tell you whether a developer can solve problems, think logically, or write efficient code. These skills are essential for success in any programming role.

Using a computer programmer aptitude test helps you evaluate:

- Coding fundamentals

- Analytical and logical reasoning

- Problem solving ability

- Learning speed

- Communication skills within technical problem contexts

This approach saves time because you only move candidates with verified technical skills to the interview stage.

Modern assessment platforms like iMocha offer a wide range of tests that help evaluate developers across programming languages, frameworks, and soft skills. iMocha has more than 3,000 skills assessment tests which include more than 690+ IT and programming tests. The platform also supports remote proctoring through image and browser monitoring which helps maintain test integrity.

## Should You Prioritize Experience?

Many HR teams wonder whether experience should be the deciding factor. The answer depends on what you are trying to achieve.

A candidate with years of experience may not always have strong technical depth. A fresher or junior candidate may show stronger logic and problem solving skills.

This is why validated skills matter more than years of work experience. Use application oriented assessments that evaluate coding ability, debugging skills, algorithmic thinking, and practical scenarios. These tests help you compare candidates fairly and identify those who can actually perform the job.

## Resume Screening Still Matters, but Use It Wisely

While technical tests give you objective data, resumes still play a role. With AI resume screening, look for elements that show initiative and continuous learning, such as:

- Certifications

- Side projects or open source contributions

- Participation in hackathons or coding forums

- Knowledge of multiple programming languages

- Clean formatting that shows attention to detail

Many programmers prefer to express themselves through their code rather than a polished resume. This is why skills based assessments provide a more accurate picture than judging a resume alone.

## Key Programming Skills to Look For

Most programmers should have a foundation in at least one core language along with broader technical knowledge.

### Technical Skills

- Fundamentals of C, C++, Java, C Sharp, Python, or PHP

- HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and basic front end concepts

- Database fundamentals

- SQL basics

- Understanding of software development practices

- Basic knowledge of web frameworks or libraries

### Soft Skills

- Analytical thinking

- Logical reasoning

- Critical thinking

- Clear communication

- Team collaboration

These skills influence a programmer’s ability to work with colleagues, understand requirements, and contribute to projects effectively.

## How to Assess These Skills

Combine a technical aptitude test with job role specific programming assessments. You can evaluate candidates across both coding and workplace competencies.

For example:

- SQL online tests

- C or C++ coding skills test

- Advanced Java assessments

- Python coding test

- C Sharp test

- PHP assessments

- Customer focus or communication competency test

Platforms like iMocha allow you to bundle multiple assessments into one test. This helps you evaluate technical and behavioral strengths in a single sitting. You also receive detailed reports that help you understand performance across each section and skill.

These reports typically offer:

- Overall score analysis

- Section level performance

- Skill wise breakdown

- Time taken and accuracy metrics

This makes it easy for a non technical recruiter to understand a candidate’s strengths.

## Conducting the Personal Interview

After shortlisting candidates based on skills assessments, move candidates to the interview stage. If you do not have programming experience, involve a technical colleague or hiring manager who can evaluate deeper technical decisions.

During the interview, focus on behavioral and practical questions such as:

- Can you walk me through a project you completed and explain your approach?

- Are you active on coding forums or platforms? Can you share examples of your work?

- How do you handle feedback or code reviews from teammates?

- What excites you most about programming?

- When do you feel most productive at work?

- How do you ensure that you meet project deadlines?

These questions help you understand mindset, attitude, teamwork, motivation, and clarity of communication. Speed up hiring and get unbiased, data driven insights with iMocha’s automated video interview solution. It helps you screen candidates efficiently even if you do not have deep technical expertise.

## Check for Cultural Fit

Technical ability alone does not guarantee success. A developer should fit your company culture and collaborate well with other team members. Ask candidates about their interests, long term goals, ways of working, and expectations from workplace culture.

A programmer who aligns with your culture is more likely to stay longer, be more engaged, and contribute positively to the team.

## Always Include a Mini Project

Before making the final hiring decision, assign a short practical task or mini project. This helps you evaluate:

- How the candidate applies theoretical knowledge

- Creativity and approach to solving real problems

- Code quality and structure

- Consistency under time constraints

If you are choosing between two strong candidates, a mini project is often the best differentiator.

## Drug Test and Background Check

Once you finalize a candidate, complete formalities such as a drug test and background verification. This ensures workplace safety, reliability, and professional conduct.

## Final Thoughts

Hiring programmers without technical expertise is completely possible when you follow a structured, skills based hiring approach. Using assessments before interviews helps you shortlist the right candidates and saves valuable time. With clear evaluation steps, you can confidently hire programmers who are skilled, reliable, and a strong fit for your organization.

## FAQs

### 1. Can iMocha help me assess programmers even if I do not understand coding?

Yes. iMocha provides ready to use programming assessments that automatically evaluate code quality, logic, accuracy, and problem solving. The platform scores responses for you, so you can shortlist skilled programmers without needing technical knowledge.

### 2. What types of programming tests does iMocha offer?

iMocha offers more than 3,000 skill assessments including more than 600 IT and programming tests. These cover languages like Java, Python, C Sharp, C++, JavaScript, PHP, SQL, and many others. You can also choose role based tests for software developers, QA engineers, and full stack developers.

### 3. Can I customize coding assessments in iMocha for specific job roles?

Yes. iMocha allows full customization of assessments. You can add or remove skills, set the difficulty level, include case studies, and combine technical and behavioral competencies in a single test that fits your job description.

### 4. How does iMocha prevent cheating during online coding tests?

The platform uses remote proctoring features such as webcam monitoring, browser activity tracking, and window violation alerts. This helps ensure test integrity and gives you confidence that the results reflect a candidate’s true ability.

# How to Interview Senior Software Engineer in 2026

Table of contents
Text Link

The demand for hiring qualified tech talent in the IT industry has been increasing for a while. With more industries and businesses going digital due to technological advancements, the need for top-notch tech experts is growing yearly.$

/$

However, as the demand for hiring top software engineers continues to rise, filling tech roles becomes even more challenging. A survey revealed that 86% of hiring managers and technical recruiters need help finding and hiring software engineers.

According to IDC, software engineers have become a valuable resource for any industry or company due to the shortage of full-time developers, which is projected to increase from 1.4 million in 2021 to 4.0 million in 2025.

This creates numerous hiring challenges in the IT industry, making it difficult to fill positions with skilled tech professionals.$

/$

As a result, many are seeking better ways how to interview senior software engineer. However, before we dive into that, it's important to examine some of the main challenges that tech recruiters face.$

/$

Now, the question remains, “how to interview senior developer” so all functional and technical aspects are thoroughly assessed. But that, too, comes with a few challenges:‍

Challenges you might encounter as you build your tech team

- Limited pool of candidates with relevant technical skills

- Market competition

- Time-consuming interviews

- High costs of hiring software engineers

- Lack of formal IT education

Now that we mentioned the common engineer hiring challenges, here’s how to interview senior software engineer with planning and tweak how you strategize the hiring process.

## 1.Here are a few ways on how to interview senior software Engineer

### I. Live coding interviews

Live coding interviews are challenges or exercises that mimic real work a candidate might do on the job. The candidate is assessed in a pair programming interview, in which they will interact directly with the existing tech team on a project. Some of its benefits are:

- Live coding interviews make the most sense if you want to hire for a coding-only position. This method is best for assessing senior role positions, which require a lot more than coding abilities. It evaluates how someone thinks through code and approaches problems and how they will lead others.

- The coding challenges typically include something close to what the candidate would do on the job. The candidate can also complete the challenge in a reasonable amount of time.

- Candidates can’t cheat with live coding. The skills demonstrated by them are completely practical. For example, a candidate may have mentioned they know what a singleton pattern is, but do they know how to write one or recognize one in a code?

Live coding interviews help track precisely this! The candidate will apply their knowledge and walk the technical interviewer through their work in detail.$

/$

Some other skills you can check during a live coding interview include:

- Oral communication: how easily can a candidate explain their thought process or understanding of the coding challenge?

- Openness to feedback or different opinions: how do they take feedback or criticism from the interviewers?$

/$
